On 2026-07-24, the selected area (centered near 40.355°, -4.514° in central Spain) experienced intense wildfire activity [5, 6]. Satellites recorded 1,232 active fire detections across an observational footprint of approximately 531.10 km² [5, 6]. The total radiative energy mapped for this single day reached 47,180.05 GJ, corresponding to an estimated 17,362.26 tonnes of dry biomass consumed [1, 6]. Summed fire radiative power across all sensor overpasses totaled 56,169.64 MW, with individual peak detection powers reaching up to 1,509.7 MW observed by Aqua [5].

Contextual profiling indicates this date was part of a larger, 5-day burning episode spanning from 2026-07-23 through 2026-07-27, which peaked on 2026-07-25 and generated an integrated total of 222,055.62 GJ of fire radiative energy [1, 6]. While satellite observations confirm substantial, rapid thermal activity consistent with a major wildland fire, orbital sensors do not document ignition sources or local emergency response; official dispatch logs or ground incident reports would be required to establish the specific ignition cause and operational fire perimeter [5].

emission_assumptions.status: PM2.5 requires measured annual fuel classes and supported factors. CO2 uses an assumed constant factor; neither is measured emissions.

episode_summary.method: Dashboard full-history calibrated daily FRE integrated over the cells represented each day, with industrial exclusion (<0.75); robust same-month median + 3 scaled MAD, at least 5% of peak. Candidate counts use <=0.75. Duration is consecutive thermal activity within ±15 days, not official incident duration.

items.label: Total radiative energy
items.formula: Σ daily FRE (MJ/km²) × represented cell area (km²) ÷ 1,000 over 1 days = 47,180.055 GJ

verified_calculations.note: Energy is a model-derived estimate from sampled satellite observations, not a continuous physical measurement. Biomass uses the Wooster combustion factor of 0.368 t per GJ.
